licensingConstraints.constraint: Procedural or original illustrations only (license original-swoond); no third-party photographs of pots, potters, museum objects, studios or kilns.
Original or synthesized studio sounds (ring test, kiln ticks and pings, wheel) only; no TV, video or podcast audio.
Clay, kiln, wheel and glaze brands, NCECA and TV titles appear as text mentions and link-outs only, no logos.
No embedded show or clip video; deep-link to official pages.
Publisher article text, museum catalogue text and glaze recipe sets are never copied; Swoon'd writes its own examples and links to sources (spec sections 11 and 40).

FDA and CPSC are public US-government sources; verify current terms and rate limits at adapter build; OpenStreetMap requires ODbL attribution; TVmaze and TMDB need licence review before commercial use.
Real potters, artists, judges and hosts are named as facts only; no likeness, no fabricated quotes, no endorsement implication.
Cultural heritage: living traditions (Japanese, Korean, Pueblo, Mexican and others) are described with respect; sacred, ceremonial or community-owned designs are never replicated as decoration.

safetyConstraints: Studio safety follows conservative mainstream guidance (OSHA respirable crystalline silica limits: PEL 50 ug/m3 8-hour average, action level 25 ug/m3; verify at release). Dry clay and glaze dust contain crystalline silica; teach wet cleaning, HEPA vacuums, covered clay, and never dry sweeping, blowing dust or dry sanding.

Respirators and dry-powder handling (glaze mixing, sanding) belong to trained people with proper controls; never present a paper dust mask as adequate for silica, and never encourage mixing or spraying glazes at home without training.

Glaze materials include hazardous substances (barium carbonate, lithium, manganese, chromium, cadmium and selenium colorants, nickel, lead frits); teach hygiene (wash hands, no food or drink in the studio) and to ask the studio; no medical advice.

Kilns reach roughly 1,800 to 2,400 F and carry burn, fire and fume risks (sulfur, carbon monoxide from fuel-fired kilns, organic burnout). Only trained people load, fire and unload kilns; never open or unload a hot kiln; never teach home kiln installation, wiring or firing; raku and atmospheric firing are taught as understanding, never as a how-to.

'Food safe' requires a lead-free, properly formulated, fully melted, well-fitted glaze; lead and cadmium can leach from crude, antique, imported or decorative ware (FDA guidance). Teach to ask the maker and to avoid using decorative, crude, antique or unknown-source ware for food or drink; Swoon'd never certifies ware.
Sharp trimming tools and cutting wire: no speed scoring and no gamified tool handling. Never gamify safety topics with timers or streak pressure.

Swoon'd builds appreciation and understanding, not a substitute for studio instruction; never encourage the learner to fake pottery skill, claim credit for a piece they did not make, or use her studio, kiln or materials without her studio's training.
